# Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 46 (Bu-Vb Pc46)

**ID:** Bu-Vb Pc46
**Section:** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga (bu-vb)
**Collection:** Vinaya
**Title (Pali):** Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 46
**Title (English, from literature):** Visiting families before a meal
**tipitaka.org (CST):** https://tipitaka.org/romn/cscd/vin02m1.mul0.xml

## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and catalog data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Cārittasikkhāpada* (Bhikkhu Vibhaṅga Pācittiya 46) regulates monks' visits to households in connection with an invitational meal [Vinaya Pitaka vol 4 - Mahavagga]. Under this rule, a monk who has accepted an invitation to a meal (*nimantita*) commits an offense of expiation (*pācittiya*) if he calls upon lay families before or after that meal without having asked permission (*anāpucchā*) from another monk who is present, except on allowable occasions [Vinaya Pitaka vol 4 - Mahavagga; Hüsken 1997]. A recognized exception is the season for making robes, which commentary connects to the privileges of the *kaṭhina* period that allow monks to visit families without having asked leave (*anāmantacāra*) [Vinaya Pitaka vol 4 - Mahavagga; Hüsken 1997].
